items.title: Is Verizon Stock Cheap, Or Just Done Growing?
items.summary: Verizon Communications (VZ) trades at about 12 times earnings, against an S&P 500 median of 22.4. A discount that wide usually follows a collapse. Not here. The stock returned 14.1% over the past twelve months, behind the index's 17.9%, and management has raised parts of its 2026 guidance in two straight quarters. So is this a good business on sale or a fair price for a company that has stopped growing.

items.title: Verizon plans to discontinue a phone service customers rely on
items.summary: Verizon is seeking approval to end a longtime service that could affect customers in several states.

items.title: How Far Can Comcast Stock Fall, And How Long Would You Wait?
items.summary: Comcast (CMCSA) trades near $22, about 29% below its 52-week high, and the market has not been falling with it. The S&P 500 returned close to 18% over the past year, while Comcast lost about 21%. The company is in the middle of a broadband pivot that it says is holding its own results down. So the question is not how hard Comcast drops in a crisis. It is how long it stays down.

items.title: Verizon Commits $70 Million to Nationwide AI Training Initiative
items.summary: Verizon (NYSE:VZ) said it is investing $70 million in a nationwide initiative aimed at providing artificial intelligence training to job seekers, small businesses and educators in the United States. The telecommunications company is working with non-profit organisations including Goodwill Industries and aims to provide AI training to hundreds of thousands of people.

items.title: Verizon Seen Leading 2027 Spectrum Auction, With SpaceX Lurking
items.summary: Verizon could spend up to $20 billion in a 2027 spectrum auction, says analyst, while SpaceX participates cautiously amid Starlink expansion.

items.title: 3 Dividend Stocks Trading Cheap Enough to Buy Meaningful Stakes for Under $1,000
items.summary: AT&T, Verizon, and Pfizer all trade under $50 a share, but a low entry price and genuine value are two very different things, and only one of these three high-yield names carries a coverage story that should make income investors nervous.

items.title: Meta Platforms’ Petal Cable Puts Corning at the Center of AI’s Bandwidth Boom
items.summary: Meta Platforms unveiled Petal, a petabit-scale subsea cable linking the U.S. and France, boosting demand for optical infrastructure suppliers like Corning amid AI-driven data center buildouts.
